messages:
sam: Hey folks, urgent help please. Partner needs an ocular prosthesis after enucleation next week. Supplier is out-of-network and insurer pended for "no prior auth". Is there a fast-track for single-case exception?
hannah: Sorry to hear that, Sam. We can request an expedited prior auth or a medical necessity exception. DM me the member ID and supplier quote with HCPCS (e.g., V2627) and we'll start a case.
benefits-bot: Hi Sam 5 please submit pre-auth at https://benefits.redwood.example.com/preauth and attach: 1) itemized supplier quote, 2) ocularist evaluation, 3) surgeon letter of medical necessity. Mark "Expedite" and include procedure date. Typical expedited turnaround 72 hours.
raul: Also ask the supplier for a brief geographic access statement if they say no in-network supplier is available. That strengthens a single-case agreement. I can run a network lookup if needed.
sam: DM sent with member ID and vendor quote. Vendor included HCPCS and said they can bill insurer if payer accepts direct billing.
kate-caseworker: Process note 5 after you submit the pre-auth, email people-ops@redwood.com with subject "URGENT: ocular prosthesis Member 6XXXXX" so we create a manual case. We'll assign a case manager and chase provider relations if insurer is slow.
hannah: If you want an OOP estimate too, request a pre-determination at the same time. That way member has expected EOB and can decide about paying upfront if needed.
raul: I'll run the network search and draft a short memo if there's no nearby in-network ocularist. If insurer stalls >48 hrs, escalate to provider relations.
sam: Thanks 5 vendor uploaded final invoice and access statement to DM. Sending the form now.
kate-caseworker: Case created: PA-2026-2044. Assigned to kate-caseworker. ETA for expedited review: 72 hours. I'll post insurer acknowledgement here.
sam: Appreciate everyone 5 will update when insurer replies. :pray:
